newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian court rejects cruelty case against nuns.
newsitem.headline: Australian court rejects cruelty case against nuns.

text.p: An Australian woman who claimed she was beaten and abused by nuns at a Catholic orphanage in the 1950s was told on Tuesday she had left it too late to bring legal action against them.
"They've beaten me again," said Margaret Landsdown after the New South Wales state Supreme Court ruled it could not set aside time limits to hear her case against the Sisters of Mercy order.

In a statement to the court, Landsdown alleged that nuns at the small-town orphanage she was brought up in had tied her over an ants' nest, pushed her into a bull's paddock where she was gored and made her wear a cow's tail around her neck.

She also alleged she had been doused with boiling water, hung upside down on a clothes line, locked in cellars, forced into a hot baker's oven, hit in the face so hard by a nun that her nose broke and force-fed castor oil.
The Sisters of Mercy denied the allegations.

The Sydney court on Tuesday ruled that Landsdown had failed to meet the requirements to mount a case and said the Sisters of Mercy would find it difficult to mount a defence since most of the nuns and staff involved in the alleged abuse had since died.
Landsdown lived at the rural orphanage in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
